The Debate over the Labour Congress
Menshevik Stance (Axelrod, Larin)
"We have no party, only an organization
of petty-bourgeois intellectuals."
Propose dissolving the Social-Democratic
party into a broad, non-party
"Toilers League" to accommodate the
backward masses.
Bolshevik Stance (Lindov, Luxemburg)
"The party is a vanguard of 150,000
advanced proletarians."
A Labour Congress would artificially
disorganize the party, subject workers to
bourgeois democracy, and liquidate the
independent political force of the working
class.

The Vanguard
The Leader

front ranks, occupying the points most
heavily under fire, shedding one's blood,
but at the same time being led by others
(the bourgeois democrats).

struggle, directing it towards its goal.

The Shifting Tactics of Oil Capital
Before: The Illusion of Order
"European-style relations." Rhetoric about regulating
production and putting an end to the anarchy of strikes via a
compliant, backstage conference.
After: The Reality of Reaction
When workers demanded guarantees, the oil owners launched
open attacks: introducing a 10-kopek hospital levy, shutting
down people's halls, firing advanced workers, utilizing kochis
(thugs), and enacting lockouts.
